findings.body: The close run reports TS7022 on this newly added traversal: `parentKey` and `parent` are inferred through the loop-carried `current = parent` assignment and become implicit `any` under the repository's compiler settings. This prevents the backend and the required close command from building. Add explicit types for both locals.
findings.title: Backend does not compile

findings.body: This adds `hiddenOtherLabelCount`, contrary to the coordinator's explicit ruling that the approved `{ key, label, otherLabels }` contract has no count field and that an omitted count must be carried as a trailing `and n more` entry in `otherLabels`. The added field is also absent from the API DTO at `backend/src/chat/chat.schemas.ts:162-166`, so generated clients cannot discover it. Keep the bounded-count representation inside `otherLabels` and remove this contract extension.
findings.title: Not done: bounded names use the approved rowLabels contract

findings.body: The new disclosure uses Tailwind 3's generic `ease-out` instead of the required shared `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` easing. Its `active:scale` transition also applies to native keyboard activation, despite the stated rule not to animate keyboard-driven actions. The component test currently hard-codes these classes, so it preserves rather than catches the failed emil-design-eng checklist behavior.
findings.title: Not done: disclosure motion follows the frontend convention

findings.body: The component test still injects completed `rowLabels` through a mocked Ask API, and the current production tree has no caller of `GlNameRepository`. Consequently there is no running-API, real-database, browser proof that resolved GL and statement labels reach the table. The task plan assigns that production crossing to GL-ANSWER-WIRING, so this remains follow-up advice rather than a blocker for this task alone.
findings.title: Later: prove labels through the running Ask stack → GL-ANSWER-WIRING
